exposure: variations in the size and shape of the uterine cavity after delivery
outcome: intractable atonic PPH unresponsive to conventional treatments
cohort: The study included 30 women who had undergone a dynamic computed tomography (CT) scan for the management of severe postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) at Kyoto University Hospital between April 2011 and March 2017.
finding: A specific subtype of atonic PPH, named "PRACE" (PPH, resistance to treatment, and arterial CE), is characterized by arterial bleeding and its location, along with the shape of the uterine cavity, which can predict the need for embolization.
